records.title: How to Use This Book
records.body:
Every build has a picture of the finished build, a block list, and a plan for every layer. Build one layer at a time, from the ground up, and you can't get lost.

How to read a layer plan

  1. Each square is one block seen from above, like a bird looking down.
  2. North is at the top. Stand on the south side of your build, face north, and the plan matches what you see.
  3. Count with the numbers on the edges. Thick grid lines are every 5 blocks.
  4. Gray shadows show the layer underneath, so you know where you are.
  5. Repeat badges (like build ×3) mean build that same layer that many times, one on top of the other.
  6. The mini 3D picture on each layer shows what your build should look like when that layer is done.
START HEREWhere Layer 1 goes. Layer 1 sits on top of the grass. Some builds also have a Ground layer. Build that one first: dig out the grass and put its blocks in, like paths and ponds.
Starter Cabin, Layer 2

Plan symbols

Full block
Place one whole block.
Log on its side
The line shows which way the log lies.
Glass
See-through blocks have a white shine line.
Bottom slab
Half-colored square, bottom half.
Top slab
Aim at the top half of the block when you place it.
Stairs
The arrow points to the tall back of the stairs (uphill).
Upside-down stairs
Hollow arrow. Place against the top half of a block.
Fence or wall
A square post. Lines show where it connects.
Glass pane or iron bars
A thin line through the square.
Door
Thick bar on the side the door sits on. Doors are 2 tall.
Trapdoor
Thin bar = open trapdoor on that side.
Lantern or torch
A small circle. Dashed ring = hanging lantern.
Flower
Colored dot with a green edge.
Redstone dust
Red lines show which way the wire runs.

records.title: Before You Build
records.body:
Master builders test big ideas in a Creative world first, then build them for real in Survival. Here's how to set up a building world on Bedrock Edition.

Make a building world

  1. Tap Play, then Create New, then Create New World.
  2. Set Game Mode to Creative so you have every block and can fly.
  3. Under Advanced, turn on Flat World so the ground is totally flat.
  4. Turn on Show Coordinates (in the Game settings). Now the top-left corner shows exactly where you're standing.
  5. Want commands like /fill and /time set day? Turn on Cheats. Creative mode and cheats both turn off achievements in that world forever. That's why builders keep a separate test world.
DID YOU KNOW?Coordinates. X is east and west, Z is north and south, and Y is how high you are. Y matters a lot when you go mining (see "Where the Ores Are" on page §ores).

Mark it out first

Carpet outline: yellow = the corner you start from, red = where the door goes

Before you build any walls, lay out the shape of your build on the ground with carpet. Carpet is cheap and easy to break, and it shows mistakes before they happen.

PRO TIPWhat does tap mean? In this book, tap means right-click on a computer, press the use button on a controller, or tap the screen.
PRO TIPCrafting math. 6 blocks make 4 stairs. 3 blocks make 6 slabs. 6 glass makes 16 panes. 4 planks + 2 sticks make 3 fences.
PRO TIPGather first. Big builds need a lot of blocks. In Survival, check the block list and collect everything before you start.

records.title: Master Build Showcase
records.sub: Some of the biggest, coolest builds ever made in Minecraft, and the people who built them.

records.title: They're Building the Whole Planet

feature.headline: They're Building the Whole Planet
feature.deck: Thousands of players are rebuilding Earth in Minecraft at real size. In August 2026, MrBeast went to see how far they've gotten.
body: It started in March 2020. A YouTuber named PippenFTS had a giant idea. Build the whole Earth in Minecraft, at real size! Each block is 1 meter, about one big step.
The project is called Build the Earth. Players pick a place they know, like their own street, and build it. Then they add it to the world.

MrBeast joined in early. In July 2020, he and about 50 other players rebuilt Raleigh, the capital of his home state, North Carolina. They did it in 24 hours. The capitol building went up in about one hour.

On August 29, 2026, his MrBeast Gaming channel posted a video called "World's Largest Minecraft Build!" MineFact, one of the project's leaders, showed him around. News reports say it has passed 1 trillion blocks. The wild part? It's still less than 1% finished.
feature.pull: 1 block = 1 meter. Your whole house could be in here.
stats: builders on the biggest team, New York City
feature.record: Guinness World Records: Biggest Minecraft project (2025)
feature.playable: You can visit it for free on Minecraft Java Edition (not Bedrock).
feature.try_it: Build your own street at real size. Measure your house in steps outside (one big step is about 1 meter), then build it block for block.

records.caption: Illustration made for this book. It shows the idea, not the real build.

records.title: Big Money Build Battles

feature.headline: Big Money Build Battles
feature.deck: MrBeast loves turning Minecraft building into a contest with real prizes. Here are three of the wildest. (MrBeast didn't make or approve this book.)

cards.title: $2 VS $16,000 Minecraft House!
cards.text: Builders got paid different amounts, from a few dollars up to $16,000. The $16,000 team built a whole city with a giant MrBeast statue and a copy of a MrBeast Burger restaurant.
cards.twist: A $5,000 medieval city won, 35 points to 34. The cheaper build beat the most expensive one!

cards.title: If You Build a House, I'll Pay For It!
cards.text: Fans built houses they wished they could live in. A player named SaveMrSquishy built a Christmas house inside a giant glass ball.
cards.twist: The winner wasn't a pro. It was a fan, and the prize was a real house! Minecraft YouTuber Tubbo came in second.

cards.title: $1 vs $25,000 Build Challenge
cards.text: Pro builders got budgets from $1 all the way up to $25,000, and each one had a theme to build.
cards.twist: A builder called IcyBuildsMC won. This video brought the MrBeast Gaming channel back after a break.

feature.lesson: The big lesson: a great idea can beat a giant budget. Plan your build, pick a palette (a small team of blocks, page [[p:palette]]) and add details. That's what judges notice.
feature.try_it: Hold your own build battle with a friend. The rules are at the end of this Showcase.
links: Watch: If You Build a House, I'll Pay For It!

records.caption: Illustration made for this book. It shows the idea, not the real build.

records.title: Greenfield: The Biggest City in Minecraft

feature.headline: Greenfield: The Biggest City in Minecraft
feature.deck: One player started building a city in 2011. Hundreds of builders later, Guinness World Records named it the largest city in Minecraft.
body: A player called THEJESTR started Greenfield in August 2011. The city is built at real size, and it looks a lot like Los Angeles.
It's not just buildings on the outside. Almost every building has rooms inside that you can walk through.
The airport alone took two and a half years to build. Even after all that time, the builders said the city was only about 20% done in 2022.
feature.pull: 99% of the buildings have insides you can walk through.
feature.record: Guinness World Records: Largest city in Minecraft (2022)
feature.playable: It's a free download for Minecraft Java Edition, and it's been downloaded over 1 million times.
feature.try_it: Start a city of your own. Lay out roads first, every 13 blocks, then fill each square with one building. Mix tall and short buildings.
links: See it: Greenfield on Planet Minecraft

records.caption: Illustration made for this book. It shows the idea, not the real build.

records.title: Whole Countries, One Block at a Time

feature.headline: Whole Countries, One Block at a Time
feature.deck: Two countries made real maps of their land in Minecraft, and anyone could download them.
body: Denmark was the first country built at real size. In 2014, the Danish Geodata Agency (the people who make Denmark's maps) built the whole country at 1 block per meter. Houses, roads and train tracks were all there. The map was so big it could fill about 200 movies.
The idea came from a worker who watched his son play Minecraft.
Great Britain made a map too. In 2013, an intern at Ordnance Survey, Britain's map makers, built the country from map data.
In 2014 a bigger version came out with 83 billion blocks. Each block stood for 25 meters of land.
feature.pull: Denmark's makers turned TNT off. Players still blew things up, using minecarts with TNT inside!
feature.record: Guinness World Records: Largest real-world place built in Minecraft at full scale (Denmark, 2014)
feature.playable: Neither map is on its official download page anymore.
feature.try_it: Build a map of your own neighborhood.
try_steps: Draw your streets first with gray concrete.
Use one colored block (or a few) for each house. Pick a special block, like gold, for your own house.
Add trees, a park and your school.
Ask a grown-up to check a real map with you so the streets line up.

records.title: Minecraft, Inside Minecraft

feature.headline: Minecraft, Inside Minecraft
feature.deck: A student built a working computer out of redstone. Then it ran a tiny version of Minecraft on its own screen.
body: A computer is really just a huge pile of on and off switches. Redstone can be an on and off switch too. So can you build a computer out of redstone? Sammyuri did.
Sammyuri built a giant redstone computer called CHUNGUS 2. In 2022, two helpers, Uwerta and StackDoubleFlow, joined in. Together they made it run Minecraft, inside Minecraft.

The little world on its screen is only 8 blocks wide and 8 blocks tall, with 16 kinds of blocks. It's slow, too. In a normal game, one picture would take days to draw. So they used a special super fast server.
Sammyuri built the brain of the computer between school classes.
feature.pull: It took more than 7 months to upgrade the computer so it could run Minecraft.
stats: bytes of memory (your phone has billions)
feature.playable: The world files are free for Java Edition, but they need a special server to run fast.
feature.try_it: Every giant machine starts with one wire. Build your first redstone switch.
try_steps: Put a lever on a block.
Place a line of redstone dust from the block to where you want a light.
Put a redstone lamp at the end of the line.
Flip the lever. The lamp turns on! A computer is millions of switches like this one.
Ready for more? Head to the Redstone Workshop on page §rsbasics.
links: Watch: I made Minecraft in Minecraft with redstone!

records.title: The Lost City of Atlantis

feature.headline: The Lost City of Atlantis
feature.deck: YouTuber Jeracraft built a whole city under the ocean, and it set a world record.
body: In 2017, Jeracraft wanted a big way to celebrate 300,000 subscribers. So he built Atlantis, the city from old legends, at the bottom of the sea.
The main fortress alone has more than 5 million blocks. He finished it in about two weeks.
Building underwater is extra hard. You need a way to breathe, and water gets in everywhere. One trick builders use is to empty the water out of an area, build, then fill it back up.
feature.record: Guinness World Records: Largest underwater city in Minecraft (2017)
feature.try_it: Build a glass dome like the ones in Atlantis.
try_steps: Pick a circle from the Circle Cheat Sheet on page §circles. An 11-wide circle is a good start.
Build that circle outline in glass on the ground.
Go up one layer and build the same circle again.
Keep going up with smaller circles: 9, then 7, then 5, then 3. Put 1 glass block on top to close it.
Put a sea lantern inside so it glows. Want it underwater? Build it on the ocean floor, fill the inside with sand, then dig the sand out. The water stays out!

records.caption: Illustration made for this book. It shows the idea, not the real build.

records.title: Could You Build Minecraft for a Job?

feature.headline: Could You Build Minecraft for a Job?
feature.deck: Yes! Some people get paid to build in Minecraft. Here's how the pros do it.
body: BlockWorks started in 2013 with four friends. By 2016 there were 42 people. They build worlds for Mojang, museums and charities.

Pro builders don't place every block by hand. They use tools that fill and copy big areas, a lot like the /fill and /clone commands on page §faster. BlockWorks builds in Java Edition first. Then it turns the world into a Bedrock version.
Noxcrew has made Minecraft worlds since 2011. It's an official Minecraft Partner. It also runs MC Championship, where 10 teams of 4 creators compete.
habits: Plan first. Pros sketch the build before placing a block.
Pick a palette (page [[p:palette]]) and stick to it.
Build big shapes first, then add details.
Look from far away to check the shape.
Keep practicing. Every pro started with a first house.
battle: Pick a theme, like "a house for a dragon".
Build on flat plots side by side.
A grown-up or friend judges from 1 to 10.
Give points for the idea, the details and the colors.

records.caption: Illustration made for this book. It shows the idea, not the real build.

records.title: Master Builder Secrets
records.sub: The tricks that turn plain boxes into builds people stop and stare at.

records.title: Never Build a Plain Box
records.body:
Both of these houses are the same size. One looks boring. One looks awesome. The difference is six tricks, and you can use them on almost any build.

Before: one block type, flat roof, no details
After: the exact same size
  1. Frame it. Put logs on the corners and along the top of the walls.
  2. Stand it on stone. A row of cobblestone at the bottom makes it look strong.
  3. Give it a real roof. Stairs, with a 1-block overhang past the walls.
  1. Mix blocks. Use a few blocks that go together (see the next page).
  2. Decorate windows. Trapdoor shutters and flower boxes.
  3. Decorate the doorway. A stair step, bushes and hanging lanterns.
PRO TIPThe golden rule. If a wall is flat and all one block, add something to it. Try a pillar, a window, a line of a different block, or a plant.

records.title: Pick a Block Palette
records.body:
A palette is a small team of blocks that look good together. Pick one before you build, and stick to it.

Cozy Village

Spruce Log, Oak Planks, Cobblestone, Dark Oak Planks, White Terracotta

Old Castle

Stone Bricks, Mossy Stone Bricks, Cobblestone, Andesite, Dark Oak Planks

Modern City

White Concrete, Gray Concrete, Black Concrete, Glass, Smooth Stone

Wizard Magic

Deepslate Bricks, Polished Deepslate, Purple Concrete, Block of Amethyst, Purple Stained Glass

Desert Town

Sandstone, Sand, Terracotta, Birch Planks, Orange Wool

Winter Lodge

Spruce Log, Spruce Planks, Snow Block, Stone Bricks, Light Blue Stained Glass
PRO TIPLots, some, a little. Use lots of one main block. Use some of a second block for corners and edges. Add a little bit of something special that pops.
PRO TIPDark to light. Go from dark blocks at the bottom to light blocks at the top. It looks amazing on tall walls. Builders call this a gradient.

A dark-to-light wall

Cobblestone, then andesite, then stone bricks, then smooth stone. Mix the blocks where two rows meet.

records.title: Roofs 101
records.body:
The roof is the biggest part of a house you can see. A great roof makes a great house.

Flat
Boring on houses. Great for modern builds.
Gable
Two slopes meet at the top.
Hip
Slopes on all 4 sides.
Trimmed
Upside-down stairs under the edge.

Build a gable roof

  1. Place a row of stairs along the front wall, one block outside the wall. That's the overhang.
  2. Go up one block and in one block. Place the next row. Repeat.
  3. Do the same thing on the back wall until the two sides meet.
  4. If there's a 1-block gap in the middle, fill it with slabs.
  5. Fill in the triangle walls at each end.
PRO TIPSteep or flat. Stairs make a medium slope. For a steeper roof, put a full block under each stair. For a flatter roof, use slabs.
DID YOU KNOW?Stairs turn corners. When two rows of stairs meet, the game bends the corner stair for you. Hip roofs almost build themselves.
PRO TIPPick a darker roof. A roof one or two shades darker than the walls looks the most natural.

records.title: Walls & Windows With Depth
records.body:
Real walls aren't perfectly flat. They have pillars, ledges and windows that sit back into the wall. In Minecraft, making parts stick out by one block makes a wall come alive.

Flat wall: looks like a sticker
Bumpy wall: pillars, a base and window tops
  • Pillars stick out 1 block every 4 or 5 blocks.
  • A base of stairs or a different block along the bottom.
  • Window tops made of upside-down stairs above each window.
  • Glass panes are thinner than glass blocks, so windows look set into the wall.
PRO TIPSquint test. Step back and squint at your wall. If it looks like one flat color, make something stick out.

3 window styles to steal

1. Trapdoor shutters    2. Flower box (trapdoors + flowers)    3. Arch top (upside-down stairs) with a slab shelf below

records.title: Furniture Hacks
records.body:
Minecraft doesn't have many furniture blocks, so master builders make their own out of everyday blocks.

A room made only from normal blocks
FurnitureHow to make it
TableFence post + pressure plate on top
ChairA stair facing the table
LampFence post + lantern on top
Kitchen counterBarrels with slabs on top
SinkA cauldron (fill it with a water bucket)
FurnitureHow to make it
NightstandBarrel + flower pot
RugCarpet in a pattern
BookcaseBookshelves stacked 2 high
Real seatCushions (new in 2026). They're made from wool slabs, and you can really sit on them
CupboardOpen trapdoors on a wall
DID YOU KNOW?Chairs you can’t sit on. You can’t sit on stairs in the normal game. They only look like chairs. To really sit down, use the new cushions.

records.title: Lighting & Landscaping
records.body:
Light it up

A glowstone block is hiding under the carpet in the middle of this floor

Monsters spawn in dark places. Light up every room, path and yard, and they can't spawn there. The trick is making your lights look nice.

  • Hide lights under carpet. Light shines right through carpet.
  • Lanterns on fence posts, or hanging from chains.
  • Glowing blocks like glowstone or sea lanterns in walls and ceilings.
DID YOU KNOW?Brightest blocks. Glowstone, sea lanterns, shroomlights, lanterns and jack o’lanterns are the brightest lights in the game. Torches are a tiny bit dimmer.

Landscaping

Paths, flowers, a small tree, a pond and lanterns

The ground around your build matters as much as the build. Give your build a yard, because plain grass looks unfinished.

  • Paths: mix dirt path, coarse dirt and gravel so they look walked on. Make dirt path by using a shovel on grass.
  • Flowers and short grass: use bone meal on grass to grow lots at once.
  • Bushes: a leaf block on the ground, or a bush plant.
  • Small trees: a short log with a blob of leaves.

records.title: Circle Cheat Sheet
records.body:
Round towers, domes and fountains all start with a circle. Copy these shapes block by block. Orange is the wall, light orange is the inside.

5 wide

Outline: 16 blocks per layer

7 wide

Outline: 24 blocks per layer

9 wide

Outline: 32 blocks per layer

11 wide

Outline: 40 blocks per layer

13 wide

Outline: 48 blocks per layer

15 wide

Outline: 56 blocks per layer
PRO TIPCount the rows. Every circle looks the same on all 4 sides. Build one quarter, then copy it three more times. Count from the middle out.
PRO TIPDomes. To make a dome, stack circles that get smaller as you go up: 9, then 9, then 7, then 5, then 3.

records.title: Build Faster
records.body:
Pros don't place every block one at a time. These tricks save hours.

Build tools in Creative

  1. Fill a box. With cheats on, type:
    /fill ~1 ~ ~1 ~5 ~4 ~5 stone_bricks
    You get a 5×5×5 box of stone bricks next to you. ~ means where you're standing. ~5 means 5 blocks away.
  2. Hollow box. Add hollow at the end to make walls with air inside. Great for towers and rooms.
  3. Swap blocks. End a fill with oak_planks replace cobblestone and it only changes the cobblestone.
  4. Copy a whole build. /clone copies everything between two corners to a new spot.
PRO TIPFinding a corner. Stand on the corner block and read your Position in the top-left corner (turn on Show Coordinates). The block under your feet is 1 lower on Y.

Build like a pro

  • Match both sides. Build the left half, then copy it on the right. Count blocks from the middle.
  • Odd widths. Make walls 5, 7, 9 or 11 blocks wide so the door fits right in the middle.
  • Scaffolding. In Survival, climb up scaffolding to reach high spots. Break the bottom piece and the whole tower drops.
  • Same hotbar every time. Keep your blocks in the same slots: main block, edge block, glass, lights.
  • Check from above. Fly up high and look down. Mistakes jump out.
  • Floating blocks. Blocks need something to stick to. Place a dirt block you'll break later, stick your block to it, then break the dirt.
WATCH OUTAchievements. Creative mode and cheats both turn off achievements in that world forever. Keep a separate Creative world for command building.

records.title: Starter Cabin
records.blurb: This cozy log cabin is the best first build. It's a great home for your second day, and it looks way better than a dirt hut. You'll learn three moves you'll use again and again: log corners, a stone base and a stair roof.
records.tips:
PRO TIPCheck your corners. On Layer 2, make sure the 4 log corners match the plan. If the corners are right, the whole cabin will be right.
DID YOU KNOW?Hanging lanterns. A lantern hangs down when you place it on the bottom of a block or stair. That's how the porch lanterns work.

PRO TIPChimney smoke. The campfire on top of the chimney puffs out real smoke. A slab next to it makes the top look finished.

records.title: Mini Builds
records.body:
Small builds make a big world feel alive. Put these around your village, castle or theme park. Each one is quick.

Village Well

Water in the middle, a roof on fence posts and a hanging lantern. 68 blocks, about 5 minutes.

Street Lamp

Two hanging lanterns make any path feel like a real town. 10 blocks, about 5 minutes.

Market Stall

A striped wool roof, barrels and crops for sale. 71 blocks, about 5 minutes.

Park Fountain

A glowing sea lantern hides under the water spout. 52 blocks, about 5 minutes.
PRO TIPGroup them. Put a Village Well in the middle of a square, Market Stalls around it and Street Lamps along the paths. Instant village!

records.title: Top 10 Coolest Things to Do
records.sub: The coolest things to find and do in Minecraft right now, counting down to number 1.

records.title: The Countdown
records.body:
Here are the 10 coolest adventures in Minecraft, counting down to number 1.

#10Sneak Through an Ancient Citypage §top_ancient
#9Find the Rarest Placespage §top_biomes
#8Secret Worlds, Easter Eggs and Mythspage §top_secrets
#7Build a Copper Golempage §top_golem
#6Beat a Trial Chamber and Win a Macepage §top_trial
#5Travel to the Netherpage §top_nether
#4Defeat the Ender Dragon and Get Wingspage §top_end
#3Find Diamondspage §top_diamonds
#2Explore Sulfur Cavespage §top_sulfur
#1Tame and Fly a Happy Ghastpage §top_ghast
PRO TIPDanger meter. Each adventure has a danger meter from 1 to 5. Start with the low ones and work your way up.

Everything in this part was checked for Bedrock Edition, version 26.51 (September 2026).

item.title: Sneak Through an Ancient City
item.why: Deep underground, spooky stone cities hide some of the rarest treasure in the game. They also hide the Warden, the toughest mob in the game.
item.where: In the deep dark, around Y -51, often under mountains.
steps: Bring wool blocks to put down, so your steps stay quiet.
Sneak everywhere. Crouch-walking makes almost no noise.
Don't step on sculk shriekers (the bony-looking blocks). Four shrieks call the Warden.
Grab loot from chests fast and leave the same way you came.
need: Snowballs (throw them to make a distraction)
item.wow: The Warden is blind. It finds you by feeling vibrations and by smell. If it can't sense you for a minute, it digs back underground.
item.note: The Swift Sneak enchantment, which makes sneaking faster, only comes from ancient city chests.

item.title: Find the Rarest Places
item.why: Some parts of the world are so rare that most players never see them.
places: A gray, silent forest. At night, creakings come out. A creaking only moves when you're not looking at it. Hitting it does nothing. Break the creaking heart hidden in a pale oak log instead.
Pink trees and falling petals on the sides of mountains. Totally safe and very pretty.
Islands far out at sea with giant mushrooms and mooshroom cows. Monsters don't spawn there, so it's one of the safest places to live.
steps: Explore in one straight direction. Rare places are often far away.
Look for treasure maps. Since the Wilderness Bound drop (September 2026), chests in abandoned camps can hold maps to cherry groves and pale gardens.
Sail a boat to find mushroom islands.
need: A bed to set your spawn
item.wow: Mushroom fields are only about 0.15% of a world. Lightning can turn a red mooshroom brown!

records.title: Secret Worlds, Easter Eggs and Myths

item.title: Secret Worlds, Easter Eggs and Myths
item.why: Every player wants to know: are there secret worlds, hidden jokes, or ghosts? Here's the truth.
eggs: Name a mob Dinnerbone (or Grumm) and it flips upside down.
Name a sheep jeb_ and its wool cycles through a rainbow.
Name a rabbit Toast and it gets a black and white coat. It's a tribute to a player's pet bunny.
item.rare: A blue axolotl has a 1 in 1,200 chance when you breed axolotls. Pink sheep are about 1 in 600. Brown pandas are the rarest pandas.
myths: No. There are only three: the Overworld, the Nether and the End. A "Sky Dimension" was planned a long time ago, but it was never added.
No. Herobrine is a made-up spooky story. He was never in the game, but the makers still joke about him.
Very old versions had glitchy, broken land super far away. You can't reach it in today's Bedrock.
steps: Craft a name tag with paper and any nugget (new in 2026).
Use an anvil to write the name. It costs 1 experience level.
Use the name tag on the mob.
item.wow: The ancient city has a giant frame that looks like a portal. It's just decoration.

item.title: Build a Copper Golem
item.why: The copper golem is a little helper that sorts your stuff. It lost a mob vote in 2021, but it finally came to the game in 2025!
steps: Place a Block of Copper (made from 9 copper ingots).
Put a carved pumpkin on top. The golem pops out, and the copper block turns into a copper chest.
Put items in the copper chest. The golem carries them to wooden chests nearby and sorts them.
need: A carved pumpkin (use shears on a pumpkin)
item.wow: Over time it turns green and can freeze into a statue. Scrape it with an axe to clean it, then use the axe again to wake it up. Rub honeycomb on it to stop it from turning green.
item.note: Iron golems sometimes give copper golems a poppy to wear.

records.title: Beat a Trial Chamber and Win a Mace

item.title: Beat a Trial Chamber and Win a Mace
item.why: Trial chambers are copper dungeons full of monster waves, locked treasure boxes and the super strong mace.
item.where: Underground, around Y -40 to -20. A cartographer villager can sell you a map.
steps: Find a trial spawner and defeat every wave of mobs.
Collect the trial key it drops.
Use the key on a vault to get treasure. Each player can open each vault once.
Ominous vaults can give a heavy core. To open one, drink an ominous bottle first, then beat the spawners for an ominous key. Heavy core + breeze rod = a mace!
item.wow: The mace hits harder the farther you fall before you swing. Land a smash and you take no fall damage.
item.note: Breezes knock arrows away, so fight them up close.

item.title: Travel to the Nether
item.why: The Nether is a fiery world full of lava, glowing blocks and a super rare treasure: netherite.
item.where: You make your own door to it: a Nether portal.
steps: Build an obsidian frame 4 blocks wide and 5 blocks tall. You can skip the 4 corners, so you only need 10 obsidian.
Light the inside with flint and steel. Step in and wait.
For netherite, find ancient debris around Y 15 with a diamond pickaxe.
Smelt it into scrap. 4 scrap + 4 gold ingots = 1 netherite ingot.
need: At least one piece of gold armor (piglins leave you alone)
item.wow: 1 block walked in the Nether equals 8 blocks in the Overworld. Players use the Nether as a shortcut!
item.note: Build a tall pillar next to your portal so you can find your way home. And never sleep in a bed there. It explodes!

records.title: Defeat the Ender Dragon and Get Wings

item.title: Defeat the Ender Dragon and Get Wings
item.why: The Ender Dragon is the big boss of Minecraft. Beat it and you can explore floating cities and find elytra, wings that let you glide.
item.where: In the End. Find the portal inside a stronghold, deep underground.
steps: Throw eyes of ender. They fly toward the nearest stronghold.
Fill the End portal frame with eyes of ender (12 spots) and jump in.
Break the glowing crystals on top of the pillars first. They heal the dragon.
Defeat the dragon. A small gateway portal appears. Throw an ender pearl into it.
Explore End cities. Elytra hang on the wall of End ships.
need: A bow and lots of arrows
A carved pumpkin to wear (endermen won't attack)
item.wow: With elytra on, firework rockets launch you like a jet, about 33 blocks every second!

item.title: Find Diamonds
item.why: Diamonds make super strong tools and armor. Your first diamond feels amazing!
item.where: Deep down, near Y -58 or Y -59.
steps: Make an iron pickaxe. Weaker pickaxes break diamond ore and give you nothing.
Dig a staircase down to Y -58. Never dig straight down.
Dig long tunnels at that level. Tunnels find more diamonds than caves do.
Watch out for lava. It's very common down there.
item.wow: Diamonds next to open air are less likely to form. That's why tunnel digging works so well.
item.note: See the ore chart on page §ores for where every ore likes to hide.

item.title: Explore Sulfur Caves
item.why: Sulfur caves are the newest caves in the game (June 2026). They're home to the bouncy sulfur cube.
item.where: Underground, at about the same depth as lush caves. Sulfur springs on the surface are a clue that a cave is below.
steps: Find a big sulfur cube. It's friendly.
Give it a block to swallow. The block changes how it moves.
Wood makes it bounce like a rubber ball. Ice makes it slide like a hockey puck. Wool makes it float like a beach ball.
Use shears to take the block back out.
item.wow: Hit a big cube and it splits into little ones. You can even carry a big cube in a bucket.
item.note: They live in sulfur caves. Gas from sulfur pools also makes your screen wobble.

records.title: Tame and Fly a Happy Ghast

item.title: Tame and Fly a Happy Ghast
item.why: A giant, friendly, flying ghast that you can ride with your friends. It flew into the game in June 2025.
item.where: Start with a dried ghast block. Find one near Nether fossils in soul sand valleys, or craft one with ghast tears and soul sand. Going to the Nether? See page [[p:top_nether]].
steps: Put the dried ghast in water. After about 20 minutes, a baby ghast, called a ghastling, pops out.
Wait for it to grow up. Feeding it snowballs makes it grow faster.
Craft a harness (3 leather, 2 glass and 1 wool) and put it on the grown-up ghast.
Climb on! Look where you want to go and move forward. Jump to fly higher.
item.wow: Up to 4 players can ride one happy ghast at the same time.
item.note: Getting a dried ghast from the Nether is dangerous. The ghast itself is gentle.

records.title: What's New in Minecraft
records.body:
Minecraft gets new updates, called game drops, a few times a year. Here's what came out lately, so you know what to look for.

March 2025

Spring to Life

Fallen leaves, wildflowers and bushes, plus warm and cold versions of farm animals.
June 2025

Chase the Skies

The happy ghast, a friendly ghast you can ride through the sky. Saddles became craftable.
September 2025

The Copper Age

The copper golem, copper chests, copper tools and armor, and the shelf block.
December 2025

Mounts of Mayhem

Spears, a nautilus (a shelled sea animal) you can ride underwater, and netherite horse armor.
March 2026

Tiny Takeover

New looks for baby mobs, name tags you can craft, and a copper block under a note block plays a trumpet.
June 2026

Chaos Cubed

Sulfur caves, the bouncy sulfur cube mob, and geysers (steam vents) that launch you into the air.
September 2026

Wilderness Bound

Cushions you can sit on, straw beds, poplar trees, abandoned camps, and wool and concrete stairs and slabs.
DID YOU KNOW?Where to find new stuff. New mobs and items show up right away when the game updates. New caves, trees and plants only appear in places you haven’t explored yet, so go somewhere new! This book was checked against version 26.51 (September 2026).

records.title: Survival Hints
records.sub: Stay alive, find diamonds, grow food and make friends with villagers.

records.title: Your First Day
records.body:
Your first 20 minutes are an adventure. Follow this list and you'll sleep safe on night one.

  1. Punch a tree. Collect about 10 logs. Turn them into planks and sticks.
  2. Crafting table. 4 planks. This unlocks the big 3×3 crafting grid.
  3. Wooden pickaxe. 3 planks + 2 sticks. Use it to mine some stone.
  4. Stone tools. Make a stone pickaxe, sword and axe. They are much faster.
  5. Find food. Hunt animals, grab apples that drop from oak leaves, or pick sweet berries.
  6. Coal and torches. Coal is easy to spot in rock. 1 coal + 1 stick = 4 torches.
  7. Shelter before dark. You get about 10 minutes of daylight. Build walls, a roof and a door.
  8. Make a bed. 3 wool (from sheep) + 3 planks. Sleeping skips the night and sets your spawn point.
Out of time? A 5×5 dirt hut with a door and torches is fine for night one. Upgrade to the Starter Cabin tomorrow!
WATCH OUTPhantoms. If you go 3 days without sleeping, phantoms start swooping at you at night. Sleep to reset the count.
WATCH OUTBed rules. Beds only work in the Overworld. In the Nether and the End, a bed explodes when you try to sleep!

records.title: Where the Ores Are
records.body:
Every ore has a favorite depth. Check your Y number and dig at the right level. The shaded bar shows where each ore can appear. The outlined stripe is the best spot.

PRO TIPDiamonds. Dig tunnels at Y -58 or -59. You need an iron pickaxe or better to mine them.
PRO TIPIron. Most common around Y 16, and again high up in mountains around Y 232.
PRO TIPEmeralds. Only found inside mountains. The higher up in the mountain you dig, the better.
DID YOU KNOW?Nether treasure. Ancient debris (for netherite) is most common at Y 15 in the Nether. Mine it with a diamond pickaxe.

records.title: Mining Smart
records.body:
Branch mining

Seen from above: one main tunnel, with side tunnels 3 blocks apart
  1. Go down to your target depth using a staircase, never straight down.
  2. Dig a main tunnel 2 blocks tall.
  3. Every 3 blocks, dig a long side tunnel. You'll see the ore hiding in between.
  4. Put torches on your right side going in. On the way out, they're on your left.

Mining safety

WATCH OUTNever dig straight down. You could fall into a cave, a lava pool or a crowd of monsters.
WATCH OUTLava is common deep down. Deep caves are full of lava. If you hear bubbling or see orange light, slow down.
PRO TIPCarry a water bucket. Water turns lava into obsidian or cobblestone. It puts out fire on you. Pour it under you to stop fall damage.
PRO TIPPack your bag. Bring a spare pickaxe, food and torches. Add a stack of blocks to wall off lava, and a bed if you plan to stay.
DID YOU KNOW?Pickaxe order. Wood, then stone, then iron, then diamond, then netherite. You need an iron pickaxe to mine gold, redstone and diamonds.

records.title: Food & Farming
records.body:
Food power rankings

The brown squares show how much a food fills your hunger bar. The yellow bar shows how long it keeps you full. You can't see the yellow bar in the game, but it's there! Foods are ranked by the yellow bar.

FoodFills hungerKeeps you full
Golden carrot
Steak

Rabbit stew
Cooked mutton
Cooked salmon
Cooked chicken
Bread
Baked potato
Pumpkin pie
Carrot
Apple
Sweet berries
PRO TIPBest food. Golden carrots keep you full the longest. Steak and cooked porkchops are great everyday food.

Farming 101

A 9×9 farm with one water block in the middle waters every crop
  1. Use a hoe on dirt or grass to make farmland.
  2. Water keeps farmland wet up to 4 blocks away.
  3. Plant seeds. Crops grow faster with bone meal.
  4. Harvest when wheat turns golden. 3 wheat = 1 bread.
  5. Put a fence around it so animals don't stomp on it.

records.title: Mob Survival Guide
records.body:
Know your enemy! Here's what the most common monsters do, and the best way to deal with each one.

Creeper

Danger: Hisses when it gets close, then explodes about 1.5 seconds later.

Beat it: Back away fast. If you get about 7 blocks away, it stops. Creepers are scared of cats.

Zombie

Danger: Slow, but comes in groups at night.

Beat it: Zombies burn in sunlight. Stay inside with the door shut until morning. On Hard, zombies can break wooden doors, so use an iron door.

Skeleton

Danger: Shoots arrows from far away.

Beat it: Hold up a shield, or get close fast. Skeletons burn in sunlight and are scared of wolves.

Spider

Danger: Climbs walls. Can jump on your roof.

Beat it: Add an overhang to your walls. Spiders are calm in bright daylight unless you hit them.

Enderman

Danger: Tall and quiet. Looking at its face makes it attack.

Beat it: Don’t stare! Wear a carved pumpkin on your head, or stand under a 2-block-high ceiling where it can’t follow.

Drowned

Danger: Lives in oceans and rivers. Some throw tridents.

Beat it: Stay out of deep water at night. Fight them from land.

Phantom

Danger: Swoops from the sky at night.

Beat it: Only shows up if you haven’t slept for 3 days. Sleep in a bed and they’ll never show up.

Monster-proof your base

  • Light up every dark spot.
  • Use doors, or fence gates for outdoor areas.
  • Build walls at least 2 blocks tall with an overhang.
  • Keep a pet cat or a tamed wolf. Creepers stay away from cats, and wolves chase skeletons.

records.title: Villagers & Enchanting
records.body:
Villager trading

Villagers trade useful stuff for emeralds. Their job depends on the job block they pick.

JobJob blockGood for
LibrarianLecternEnchanted books
FarmerComposterEasy emeralds for crops
ArmorerBlast furnaceIron and diamond armor
ToolsmithSmithing tableTools
ClericBrewing standEnder pearls, redstone
  • More villagers: villagers need free beds to have babies, plus food like 3 bread or 12 carrots, potatoes or beetroots.
  • Cheaper trades: cure a zombie villager with a splash potion of weakness and a golden apple. After that, it gives you big discounts.
PRO TIPIron golems. Villages with enough villagers make iron golems that protect them. Don’t hit a villager or the golem will come after you!

Enchanting setup

15 bookshelves = level 30 enchantments

Put bookshelves exactly 1 air block away from the table, at the same height or one higher. The gap must be empty air in Bedrock: no torches or carpet.

PRO TIPEnchant smart. Enchanting costs experience levels and lapis lazuli. Save up 30 levels before using the top choice.

Going to the Nether? See number 5 in the Top 10 on page §top_nether for how to build a portal and stay safe.

records.title: Redstone Workshop
records.sub: Doors that open themselves, lights that turn on at night, and a secret passage.

records.title: Redstone Basics
records.body:
Redstone is Minecraft's electricity. Every redstone gadget has three parts: something that makes power, something that carries it, and something that uses it.

1. Power sources

  • Lever: on or off, stays that way
  • Button: on for about a second
  • Pressure plate: on while something stands on it
  • Redstone torch: always on, unless the block it's stuck to gets powered
  • Daylight detector: on in daytime (or at night if you tap it)
  • Observer: blinks when the block in front of it changes

2. Wires

  • Redstone dust: the wire. Power gets weaker with every block and runs out after 15 blocks.
  • Repeater: boosts the power back to full strength and adds a tiny wait.
  • Solid blocks: a powered block passes power to things touching it.

3. Things it powers

  • Doors and trapdoors open
  • Redstone lamps light up
  • Pistons push blocks (sticky pistons pull them back)
  • Note blocks play a sound
  • Hoppers stop moving items
DID YOU KNOW?Bedrock redstone is different. Some redstone videos online are made for Java Edition, and those gadgets can break on Bedrock. Every gadget in this book was designed for Bedrock.
PRO TIPTry it in Creative first. Build each gadget in a Creative test world. When it works, build it for real in Survival.

Placing hoppers the right way

A hopper's spout points at the block you tapped when you placed it. To make a hopper feed into a chest or furnace, sneak (crouch) and tap that chest or furnace while you place the hopper. In the pictures, look at the little spout under each hopper to see which way it feeds.

records.title: Automatic Iron Door
records.body:
Iron doors can’t be opened by hand. Give yours a pressure plate and a button and it opens itself.

Outside: button
Inside: pressure plate

How it works

A pressed plate or button powers the blocks next to it. The iron door is right next to them, so it gets power and swings open. When the power stops, it closes.

Build it

  1. Build a wall and place an iron door in it.
  2. Inside: put a stone pressure plate on the floor right in front of the door.
  3. Outside: put a stone button on the wall block right next to the door, at chest height.
  4. Walk up and press the button. The door opens. Walk out over the plate and it opens again, then closes behind you.
PRO TIPWhy a button outside? Monsters can step on pressure plates too! A button outside means only players can get in.
PRO TIPDouble doors. Put two iron doors side by side, with a pressure plate in front of each door.
WATCH OUTKeep other gadgets apart. Keep buttons for other gadgets at least 2 blocks away from the door, or they might open it by accident.

records.title: Automatic Night Lights
records.body:
Lamps that turn on by themselves when the sun goes down. Perfect for paths, walls and rooftops.

Lamp, detector, lamp, detector, lamp

How it works

In night mode, the detector makes power when it gets dark. The lamps touching it get the power and light up. At sunrise, the power stops and they turn off.

Build it

  1. Place a row in this order: redstone lamp, daylight detector, redstone lamp, daylight detector, redstone lamp.
  2. Tap each daylight detector once. Its top changes color. That means it’s flipped to night mode.
  3. Make sure nothing is above the detectors. They need to see the sky.
  4. Wait for night, or test it in Creative with /time set night.
DID YOU KNOW?No wires needed. A daylight detector powers the lamps right next to it, so each detector lights the lamp on both sides.
PRO TIPHide the lamps. Put the whole row in the ground with the tops level with the floor for glowing path lights.
WATCH OUTNot in the Nether. Flipped detectors don’t work in the Nether. Use regular lamps with a lever there.

records.title: Note Block Doorbell
records.body:
Ding dong! A doorbell so everyone knows when a friend is at the door.

Outside: button
Inside: note block on a Block of Gold

How it works

Pressing the button powers the wall block it’s on. That block powers the note block behind it, and the note block plays.

Build it

  1. Pick a wall block 2 blocks away from your door. Put a button on the outside of it.
  2. On the inside, right behind that wall block, dig out the floor block and put in your sound block (see the chart).
  3. Place a note block on top of the sound block. It should touch the wall block.
  4. Leave the space above the note block empty, or it won’t make a sound.
  5. Tap the note block to change the note. Each tap goes one note higher.
Block under note blockSound
Block of GoldBell
Packed IceChime
ClayFlute
WoolGuitar
Block of CopperTrumpet
GlowstonePling
Hay BaleBanjo
PlanksBass
WATCH OUTKeep it away from iron doors. Put the doorbell at least 2 blocks away from an iron door, or ringing the bell will open the door!

records.title: Automatic Egg Collector
records.body:
Chickens lay an egg every 5 to 10 minutes. This pen catches every one and drops it into a chest for you.

Chickens stand on the hoppers inside a glass pen

How it works

Hoppers suck up any item that lands on top of them and pass it along the way their spout points. The eggs travel hopper to hopper and end up in the chest.

Build it

  1. Place a chest on the ground.
  2. Sneak and place a hopper on top of the chest. It feeds straight down into the chest.
  3. Add 2 more hoppers right beside the first one. Sneak and tap the first hopper as you place each one.
  4. Put the last hopper in the empty corner of the 2×2 square. Sneak and tap one of the new hoppers as you place it.
  5. Build a glass wall 3 blocks tall around the hoppers, leaving one gap.
  6. Hold seeds so chickens follow you into the pen, then fill in the gap.
PRO TIPMore chickens! Throw eggs inside the pen to hatch more chickens. More chickens means more eggs.
DID YOU KNOW?Egg uses. Eggs are used to make cake and pumpkin pie.

records.title: Auto Smelter
records.body:
Dump in a stack of raw iron and some coal, walk away, and come back to a chest full of iron ingots.

1
2
3
4
1 items to cook · 2 fuel · 3 furnace · 4 finished items

How it works

Hoppers move items from the chest above them into whatever their spout points at. The bottom hopper pulls finished items out of the furnace.

Build it

  1. Place a chest on the ground for the finished items.
  2. Sneak and place a hopper on top of the chest (feeds down).
  3. Sneak and place a furnace on top of that hopper.
  4. Sneak and place a hopper on top of the furnace. Then sneak and place a chest on top of that hopper. Put things to cook in this chest.
  5. Sneak and place a hopper on the side of the furnace, tapping the furnace. Then sneak and place a chest on top of it. Put coal in this chest.
DID YOU KNOW?Top, side, bottom. A hopper from the top fills the cooking slot. A hopper on the side fills the fuel slot. A hopper underneath takes out what’s done.
PRO TIPGo faster. Use a blast furnace for ore and a smoker for food. They cook twice as fast.

records.title: Secret Bookshelf Door
records.body:
Press a button and two bookshelves slide into the wall, opening a secret passage. When the button pops back up, the door closes and nobody will ever know.

Outside: bookshelves in a stone wall
Layer 1 (feet level)
Layer 2 (head level)
Rows 2 to 4 are the wall. Buttons go in rows 1 and 5. This is how it looks before the pistons move.

How it works

The torch is normally on, so the pistons stay pushed out and the door stays shut. The button powers the block, which turns the torch off. The pistons pull back and the doorway opens.

Build it

  1. Build a stone wall 3 blocks thick (rows 2, 3, 4), 10 long and 2 tall, leaving the empty spaces shown in the plans.
  2. Column 3 is the secret doorway. Leave it empty in all three rows.
  3. Column 5, row 3: two sticky pistons, one on top of the other. Point the slimy green sides toward the doorway (left on the plan).
  4. Column 4, row 3: put a bookshelf against each piston face.
  5. Column 7, row 3: a solid block. Stick a redstone torch on its left side (column 6). On Layer 2, put a solid block on top of the torch. The pistons push the bookshelves into the doorway. Door closed!
  6. Columns 8 and 9, row 3: redstone dust on the floor, leading into the column 7 block.
  7. Put an oak button on the outside of the column 8 wall blocks (rows 1 and 5). Press one and walk right in. The door stays open for about 1 and a half seconds.
PRO TIPTry it in Creative first. Build it in a test world before you use it in Survival. When you press the button, the torch should turn off.
WATCH OUTUse wooden buttons. Stone buttons only stay on for 1 second. That’s too fast to get through the door. Oak buttons stay on longer.
DID YOU KNOW?Only regular bookshelves. Pistons can move normal bookshelves, but not chiseled bookshelves.
